finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: attacker-supplied URL passed to file_get_contents, which accepts http, https, ftp, and file schemes. Only the response length is echoed back, so this is blind SSRF with a length oracle.
finding.source: $_POST['feed'] (import.php:12), reachable via POST import.php with no authentication (guard at import.php:11 checks only method and isset)

trace.note: Entry guard: only checks REQUEST_METHOD === POST and isset($_POST['feed']). No session or admin check on this branch.
Raw attacker value passed to file_get_contents with no scheme, host, IP, or redirect validation.
strlen of the fetched body is echoed, giving the attacker a length oracle.

finding.guards_checked: No authentication or authorization on this branch. No scheme allowlist (file:// and http:// both accepted). No host or IP block (loopback, RFC 1918, link-local, 169.254.169.254 all reachable). PHP HTTP wrapper follows redirects by default, so public-to-internal redirects bypass any initial check. No DNS pinning (rebinding possible). session_start at line 2 does not gate this branch. Assumes allow_url_fopen is enabled (PHP default); php.ini not verified.

verdict.reason: import.php:11 gates only on REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' and isset($_POST['feed']) with no session or admin check, so the raw $_POST['feed'] reaches file_get_contents at import.php:12 with no scheme, host, or IP validation, and only strlen of the response is echoed at line 13. The require_admin() guard at lines 4-9 is applied only to the set_webhook branch at line 18, not this one.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF: admin-supplied webhook URL passed to curl with no scheme or host validation. Response is discarded, so the request is blind. Admin precondition likely means this is out of scope unless admin reach exceeds in-app admin capability.
finding.source: $_POST['set_webhook'] (import.php:19), reachable via POST import.php only after require_admin() at import.php:18
finding.sink: curl_init($hook) at import.php:20 and curl_exec($ch) at import.php:22

trace.note: Branch entered when set_webhook is present in POST.
Raw value assigned to $hook with no validation.
curl_init called with the attacker-chosen URL.
curl_exec runs the request; response is not echoed.

finding.guards_checked: Admin session check present (require_admin). No scheme allowlist (libcurl defaults include file://). No host or IP restriction. No response returned, so the request is blind. Admin-only precondition weakens severity.

verdict.guard_found: none (no scheme or host validation between import.php:19 and the curl_init at import.php:20; the only guard is the admin check at import.php:18, which is an authorization gate on the source, not a validation of the URL)
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (import.php:17-22 match the claim), but the source fails the controllability check: `$_POST['set_webhook']` is reachable only after `require_admin()` at import.php:18 returns 403 for non-admin sessions, so it is admin-only input and not attacker-controlled by an unauthenticated or low-privilege user. Separately, the unauthenticated `file_get_contents($_POST['feed'])` at import.php:12 is a distinct SSRF-style sink and is not what this candidate claims.
